title: Activity-Based and Entity-Based Regulation
summary: Why the perimeter struggles with platforms that combine regulated and unregulated activities, and the arguments for activity-based rules, entity-based requirements or a combination of the two.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why the perimeter struggles with platforms that combine regulated and unregulated activities, and the arguments for activity-based rules, entity-based requirements or a combination of the two.
Learning Objectives: Compare activity-based and entity-based approaches to regulating platforms
Analyse perimeter gaps created by unregulated activities within platform groups
Evaluate group-level and holding company options for large platforms
Syllabus: Same activity, same risk, same regulation: strengths and limits
Entity-based requirements for systemically relevant platforms
FSB and BIS work on regulatory approaches to big tech
Intended Audience: Supervisors of banks, payment and e-money institutions, lenders and insurers that partner with platforms or distribute through them
Policy, innovation and authorisation staff dealing with new entrants, perimeter questions and open finance
Senior managers coordinating with competition, data protection and consumer authorities
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of banking, payments or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
